We can use the double-angle formula for cosine:

$$
{cos}^{2}⁡\theta -{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =\operatorname{cos}⁡2\theta 
$$

Therefore, 

$$
\begin{aligned}\int (3{x}^{2}-{sin}^{2}⁡x+{cos}^{2}⁡x)\text{d}x & =\int (3{x}^{2}+{cos}^{2}⁡x-{sin}^{2}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =\int (3{x}^{2}+\operatorname{cos}⁡2x)\text{d}x \\  & =3(\frac{1}{3}{x}^{3})+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x+C \\  & ={x}^{3}+\frac{1}{2}\operatorname{sin}⁡2x+C.\end{aligned}
$$
